401914105.summary: Szabová's perfect record, recent finishing power, and significant technical advantage over a declining opponent warrant backing her, but the steep -650 odds and three-round format create parlay risk.
reasons: Szabová is 12-0 with five finishes in last five fights; Lisboa is 7-4 with recent KO loss and 377-day layoff
Szabová's 4 KO wins and 5 submission wins show diverse finishing arsenal against opponent relying mainly on submissions
Under 2.5 rounds reflects Szabová's pattern of early finishes (R1 KO, R3 KO in recent fights) and Lisboa's vulnerability to strikes
Lisboa's age 35 and inactivity disadvantage against fresh 28-year-old undefeated fighter

401914106.summary: Kropschot's recent form, submission expertise, and significant reach advantage make him a strong favorite over the ring-rusty Klein, whose recent losses came via early KO.
reasons: Kropschot is 5-0 in last five with three submissions; Klein is 1-2 in last five with two early KO losses
Klein has not fought in 454 days versus Kropschot's 80 days, creating a notable activity gap
Kropschot's 79-inch reach and Team Santos Jiu Jitsu base should control distance and grappling exchanges
Klein's losses come via KO/TKO in rounds 1-2, suggesting durability and timing issues against prepared opponents

401921310.summary: Moicano's experience and submission prowess favor him, but Nolan's undefeated run, youth, size advantage, and southpaw stance create real problems; the underdog value and fight structure make totals under a better value than laying -120.
reasons: Moicano is the higher-ranked veteran with superior submission record (11 subs vs 1), but he's 37 with recent losses to elite competition
Nolan is undefeated at 11-1 with significant height and reach advantage (6'3 vs 5'11), plus southpaw angles that disrupt Moicano's orthodox stance
Moicano's last three fights went the distance or ended R2; Nolan's finishing rate is lower; under 2.5 offers better odds than laying money on aging fighter
Moicano as parlay piece is risky given age, recent top-tier losses, and opponent's undefeated record and physical attributes

401928104.summary: Luana Santos is the younger, fresher fighter with superior grappling credentials and recent consistent decision wins, but Yana's experience and striking prowess make this competitive enough that the underdog price doesn't justify parlaying her.
reasons: Luana significantly younger (26 vs 36) with more recent activity (132 vs 391 days)
Luana's judo and submission wins (6 combined) vs Yana's recent run of three consecutive decisions suggests grappling advantage
Both fighters' recent records show heavy decision-winning patterns, supporting under 2.5 rounds
Yana's age and layoff create durability questions despite +260 value

401928105.summary: Rodriguez is the more active striker with recent momentum, but Alencar's submission prowess and grappling threat make this competitive despite the heavy moneyline favoring Rodriguez.
reasons: Rodriguez wins decisively (7 of 9 wins) while Alencar relies on submissions (4 of 8 wins), suggesting Rodriguez controls pace and output over three rounds
Rodriguez has three straight unanimous decisions showing consistent point-fighting; Alencar has one decision loss indicating vulnerability to scoring-based judg
Both fighters are older (33, 36) with reach disadvantage for Alencar (58.5 vs 63.5), pointing to a controlled, grinding fight more likely under 2.5 rounds
Rodriguez moneyline at -278 carries finish risk; Alencar's submission skills create uncertainty in a heavy favorite scenario, making it poor parlay material

401928106.summary: Sezinando's recent layoff and decision-heavy finishes make him vulnerable to Berggren's aggressive KO power, but both fighters' recent losses to Donchenko and the under on rounds offers better value than the favorite moneyline.
reasons: Berggren has finished 8 of 12 wins by KO/TKO with three consecutive recent finishes, while Sezinando has only 2 decisions in last five despite facing easier com
Sezinando hasn't fought in 412 days against a hungry, active opponent coming off a recent loss looking to bounce back with aggression
Both fighters recently lost to same opponent Donchenko by early stoppage, suggesting they match similar competitive level; under 1.5 rounds avoids favorite mone

401928107.summary: Lebosnoyani's recent form and finish rate favor him, but Hasanov's undefeated record, reach advantage, and ATT pedigree make this competitive; the under 2.5 rounds is the safer play given both fighters' knockout tendencies.
reasons: Lebosnoyani riding five straight wins with three KOs and only 104 days rest, showing consistent finishing ability
Hasanov undefeated with three KOs in five fights, two recent finishes including doctor stoppage, suggesting dangerous power and aggression
Both fighters show high knockout rates (A: 27% of wins, B: 60% of wins) supporting under 2.5 rounds play
Hasanov's 2.5 inch reach advantage and ATT training could neutralize Lebosnoyani's switch stance versatility

401928109.summary: Erosa offers value as a striker with recent KO power and activity advantage against an out-of-ring opponent, but his chin concerns and Lee's submission threat create real danger.
reasons: Erosa fought 216 days ago vs Lee's 538 day layoff, significant activity edge
Erosa's last win was KO/TKO (Elkins R1) showing current striking form; Lee's last win was decision after long absence
Lee has lost two straight by KO and decision, creating momentum questions despite better record
Erosa's 9 KO losses and Lee's 4 KO wins suggest chin vulnerability, limiting parlay reliability

401931555.summary: Osbourne is fresher and slightly favored, but both fighters are aging strikers with inconsistent recent form, making the under rounds total the more predictable play than either moneyline.
reasons: Osbourne has fought more recently (251 days vs 111 days) and carries slight moneyline favor despite similar records and identical height/reach disadvantage
Both are 34-35 year old southpaw strikers with declining activity; recent form is choppy for both with Osbourne's most recent action being a no contest and Durd
Under 1.5 rounds indicates 3+ minute average fight time; given both fighters' submission and decision rates, early finishes are less likely than the over pricin

401931615.summary: Marshall's submission-heavy style and reach advantage favor him, but Hope's recent decision wins and competitive record make this competitive; the under is the cleaner play given both fighters' tendencies.
reasons: Marshall is 5-sub 1-ko with 5 subs in 10 wins; Hope is 5-dec 1-ko 1-sub with tendency toward distance and decisions
Marshall's 5-inch reach advantage (72 vs 67) and height (5'9 vs 5'6) give him leverage for clinch control and submissions
Hope's last five are all decisions or long finishes; Marshall's recent wins include a R1 submission; under 2.5 rounds aligns with their styles

401931616.summary: Smith's undefeated record, recent activity, knockout power, and reach advantage make him a justified favorite despite Brown's experience and striking credentials.
reasons: Smith is 13-0 with dominant recent finishes while Brown is 20-8 with inconsistent results and two losses in last three
Smith fought 27 days ago versus Brown's 202 days layoff, indicating better recent activity and momentum
Smith's 10 KO wins versus Brown's 3 KO losses suggests significant striking power advantage in a striker versus striker matchup
Brown is 36 years old against Smith's 30, with age typically disadvantageous in welterweight exchanges

401931617.summary: Reese is the fresher, more well-rounded fighter with better recent form, but Gall's submission skills and desperate need for a win create enough uncertainty to avoid heavy favorites; the under 1.5 rounds targets both fighters' tendency toward early finishes.
reasons: Reese significantly fresher at 111 days rest versus Gall's 713 days; Gall on four-fight skid with three KO losses suggesting serious durability concerns
Reese's 5 KO wins and 3 sub wins show balanced finishing power; Gall's six subs his only wins recently but faces opponent with 3 inches reach advantage
Both fighters' records show early finishes are common; under 1.5 rounds at minus-180 more appealing than laying minus-350 on Reese
